original_question: Let (C2, C2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype 2 operators. Does the product ideal C2* o L_infinity have property (I), meaning that for every epsilon > 0 each finite-rank operator in C2* o L_infinity can be factorized almost isometrically with one factor having finite-dimensional range?
target_in_paper: The concrete introduction-level question tied to the paper’s broader local-reflexivity agenda: whether the product ideal (\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty) has property (I), as discussed in the orbit of Conjecture 1.1 and sharpened by the nearby Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right operator ideal (the adjoint of the maximal injective cotype-2 ideal composed with \mathfrak{L}_\infty), the right structural property (property (I)), and the right qualitative meaning of that property: almost-isometric factorization of finite-rank operators with one factor forced to have finite-dimensional range.
missing_details: The question should quantify over all Banach spaces X and Y, not just over the abstract ideal.
It should specify that the finite-rank operator belongs to the component (\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)(X,Y).
It should introduce the intermediate Banach space Z through which the factorization runs.
It should specify the factorization as T=AB with A\in \mathfrak{C}_2^*(Z,Y) and B\in \mathfrak{L}_\infty(X,Z).
It should state which factor is required to have finite-dimensional range: the left factor A (equivalently, A is finite rank).
It should include the precise almost-isometric estimate from property (I), namely the product of the ideal norms being bounded by (1+\varepsilon) times the product-ideal norm of T.
To be fully stand-alone, it should say that Banach spaces are taken over the usual scalar field of the paper (real or complex).

It should name the ideals explicitly: (\mathfrak{C}_2,\mathbf{C}_2) is the maximal injective Banach ideal of cotype-2 operators, and (\mathfrak{L}_\infty,\mathbf{L}_\infty) is the ideal of \mathfrak{L}_\infty-factorizable operators.
refined_question: Let (\mathfrak{C}_2,\mathbf{C}_2) denote the maximal injective Banach ideal of all cotype-2 operators, and let (\mathfrak{L}_\infty,\mathbf{L}_\infty) denote the ideal of \mathfrak{L}_\infty-factorizable operators, over the scalar field considered in the paper. Does the canonical product ideal (\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty,\mathbf{C}_2^*\circ\mathbf{L}_\infty) have property (I); that is, for every pair of Banach spaces X,Y, every finite-rank operator T\in(\mathfrak{C}_2^*\circ\mathfrak{L}_\infty)(X,Y), and every \varepsilon>0, do there exist a Banach space Z and operators A\in\mathfrak{C}_2^*(Z,Y), B\in\mathfrak{L}_\infty(X,Z) such that T=AB, the range A(Z) is finite-dimensional, and \mathbf{C}_2^*(A)\,\mathbf{L}_\infty(B)\le(1+\varepsilon)\,(\mathbf{C}_2^*\circ\mathbf{L}_\infty)(T)?
justification: The arXiv record shows that the paper is explicitly a short note about open problems surrounding the principle of local reflexivity for maximal Banach ideals. Within that introduction-level framework, the draft is not aiming at the broad conjecture itself but at the specific cotype-2/\mathfrak{L}_\infty product-ideal question that the paper isolates nearby Conjecture 1.1 and relates to Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. So the draft is already pointed at the right narrow target; it mainly needs the full operator-ideal quantifiers and the exact norm inequality built into property (I).
